In mathematics, a '''Bratteli–Veršik diagram''' is an ordered, essentially simple [[Bratteli diagram]] (''V'',&nbsp;''E'') with a [[homeomorphism]] on the set of all infinite paths called the Veršhik transformation. It is named after [[Ola Bratteli]] and [[Anatoly Vershik]].

== Definition ==
Let ''X''&nbsp;=&nbsp;{(''e''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''e''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...) | ''e''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''E''<sub>''i''</sub> and ''r''(''e''<sub>''i''</sub>)&nbsp;=&nbsp;''s''(''e''<sub>''i''+1</sub>)} be the set of all paths in the essentially simple [[Bratteli diagram]] (''V'',&nbsp;''E''). Let ''E''<sub>min</sub> be the set of all minimal edges in ''E'', similarly let ''E''<sub>max</sub> be the set of all maximal edges. Let ''y'' be the unique infinite path in ''E''<sub>max</sub>. (Diagrams which possess a unique infinite path are called "essentially simple".) 

The Veršhik transformation is a homeomorphism φ&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''X'' defined such that φ(''x'') is the unique minimal path if ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''y''. Otherwise ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''e''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''e''<sub>2</sub>,...) | ''e''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''E''<sub>''i''</sub> where at least one ''e''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;∉&nbsp;''E''<sub>max</sub>.  Let ''k'' be the smallest such integer. Then φ(''x'') =&nbsp;(''f''<sub>1</sub>, ''f''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''f''<sub>''k''−1</sub>, ''e''<sub>''k''</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1, ''e''<sub>''k''+1</sub>,&nbsp;...&nbsp;), where ''e''<sub>''k''</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 is the successor of ''e''<sub>''k''</sub> in the total ordering of edges incident on ''r''(''e''<sub>''k''</sub>) and (''f''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''f''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''f''<sub>''k''−1</sub>) is the unique minimal path to&nbsp;''e''<sub>''k''</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1.

The Veršhik transformation allows us to construct a pointed topological system (''X'',&nbsp;''φ'',&nbsp;''y'') out of any given ordered, essentially simple Bratteli diagram. The reverse construction is also defined.

== Equivalence ==

The notion of [[Minor (graph theory)|graph minor]] can be promoted from a [[well-quasi-ordering]] to an [[equivalence relation]] if we assume the relation is [[symmetric relation|symmetric]]. This is the notion of equivalence used for Bratteli diagrams.

The major result in this field is that equivalent essentially simple ordered Bratteli diagrams correspond to [[Topological conjugacy|topologically conjugate]] pointed [[dynamical system]]s.  This allows us apply results from the former field into the latter and vice versa.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Herman |first1=Richard H. |last2=Putnam |first2=Ian F. |last3=Skau |first3=Christian F. |title=Ordered Bratteli diagrams, dimension groups and topological dynamics |journal=International Journal of Mathematics |volume=3 |issue=6 |year=1992 |pages=827–864 |doi=10.1142/S0129167X92000382 |url=}}</ref>
